section_summary.extract_value: This section reports descriptive statistics and Pearson correlations for a single study. BMI was negatively associated with body appreciation (described as a weak correlation) and positively associated with eating psychopathology (moderate magnitude); BMI was not significantly related to social safeness or self-reassurance. Social safeness and self-reassurance correlated positively with body appreciation, and body appreciation, social safeness, and self-reassurance correlated negatively with EDE-Q and its subscales.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences: "The means and standard deviations of the study variables are reported in Table 1."; "Product–moment Pearson correlation coefficients indicated that BMI revealed to be negatively associated with body appreciation and positively correlated with eating psychopathology, with weak and moderate magnitudes, respectively."; "However, a non-significant relationship was found between BMI and social safeness and self-reassurance."; "In addition, self-reassurance was significantly and positively associated, with a strong correlation, with body appreciation."
